chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Safwan from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the mukatab (slave who has agreed to pay a fixed sum for his freedom) is freed in proportion to what he pays, unless his masters stipulate that if he is unable to pay, he is returned to slavery, so the condition holds for them.

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبُ: A slave who has entered into a contract to pay a specific sum to their master in exchange for freedom.
key_terms.بِقَدْرِ مَا أَدَّى: In proportion to what he paid.

ai.seo_question: What happens to a slave's freedom status if they pay only part of their manumission price?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the principle of proportional manumission, affirming that a mukatab gains freedom commensurate with each payment installment, a view central to Shia jurisprudence on slave contracts. It also codifies the master's right to stipulate a 'total re-enslavement' clause (ruju') in case of default, highlighting the contractual flexibility within the framework of 'abd al-mukatab. This ruling underscores the balance between the slave's gradual emancipation and the master's financial security, reflecting the practical legal concerns of the early Islamic community.
